newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Benpres up on transfer of media stake.
newsitem.headline: Benpres up on transfer of media stake.

text.p: Benpres Holdings Corp rose 40 centavos, or 4.26 percent, to 9.80 pesos on Tuesday as investors viewed the transfer of its stake in media subsidiaries to parent Lopez Inc as beneficial, brokers said.

"Foreigners will now be able to invest in Benpres. Direct foreign investment is a big thing because right now Benpres' global depositary receipts are trading at a premium compared with common shares and this high price may be transferred to the common," said Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor Hagedorn Securities.
Benpres said on Monday its board had agreed to divest the company's stake in television station ABS-CBN Broadcasting Corp and cable television company Sky Vision Corp.
Philippine laws prohibit foreigners from directly investing in media companies.

"I guess foreigners view it as a positive development and for the Lopezes it's more of a strategic move since they need investments for their projects," BPI Securities Corp analyst Rosanna Tiosic said.
But Tiosic said Benpres would have to grapple with losing a cash cow in ABS-CBN, the most profitable television firm in the country.
Benpres was the third most heavily traded stock by mid-session on Tuesday.
